evidence: The original code did `.sort()` on `<date>-<shortsha>` names and took the last, so same-date pairs tie-break on an arbitrary SHA string. Accepting was right, but the fix the agent picked (generatedAt) carries the same YYYY-MM-DD string and was reopened as F14.
guidance_note: Before adopting a tie-break key, confirm it is finer-grained than the key it breaks ties on: read where generatedAt is produced (buildBaseline: `generatedAt: provenance.date`) before relying on it.

evidence: The hunk shows rev-parse and status --porcelain in one try whose catch returns `{sha: null, dirty: false}`, so a status failure throws away a SHA that was already read. Splitting the try is the right fix.
guidance_note: When one try block wraps several independent effects, give each effect its own failure path so one failure cannot erase another effect's result.

evidence: With floor ~0.2171 and 12 opportunities, `Math.ceil(floor*12)=3` gives a rate of 0.25, which is strictly above the floor, so the test named 'exactly AT the floor' never exercises the boundary. The agent confirmed this by hand and rebuilt the test at exact equality.
guidance_note: When writing a boundary test, assert the constructed input actually equals the boundary value before asserting the outcome.

evidence: The log line does `(baseline.pooledInventoryMustFind.rate * 100).toFixed(0)` and skips the null-safe pct() helper, and per the finding parseBaseline lets rate be null. Hoisting pct() so both sites share it is the right one-producer fix.
guidance_note: When a file already has a null-safe formatter, route every formatting of the same field through it instead of inlining the arithmetic.

evidence: The reviewer hedged ('I'm not fully certain this restriction hasn't been relaxed'). The agent cited the 2021-10-06 GitHub changelog, after which Dependabot-triggered runs respect the workflow `permissions:` key, so the comment is accurate. The packet only shows the agent's citation, but it matches GitHub's documented change.

The comment says DEPENDENCY_DIFF context 'helps in any repo', but per action.yml the feature only scans go.mod. The agent confirmed this and fixed the comment in the generator template (dotfiles), not in the rendered file, which is the right place.
guidance_note: When writing a rationale comment for a feature flag, check its scope against the feature's own declared description before generalizing it.

evidence: The floating @v7 tag was a deliberate, commented template decision ('first-party GitHub action where the major tag is the standard reference'), so 'a regression' overstates it. The supply-chain argument still holds: the step runs on every incoming PR before fork gating. The agent re-pinned to a SHA in the template, which is standard hardening.

The original engine check sat only in compareVerdict, after the full replay. Accepting was right, but the agent's reply promised 'refused before the first replay starts' while putting the check inside the per-case replay loop. F23 and F28 reopened that gap.
guidance_note: When a fix promises 'before any spend', put the check in a full pre-pass over every item, not inside the loop that spends, and re-read the fix against the exact promise in the reply.

evidence: expected.json changes over time, so a frozen denominator can silently mismatch. The agent added a suite-total opportunities check to compareVerdict instead of widening parseBaseline, a defensible scope choice. The check landed post-spend with no test, which caused F15 and F19.
guidance_note: When adding an incomparability guard, place it at the same pre-spend point as the sibling guards it mirrors, and add its test in the same commit.

evidence: The comment credits buildBaseline with case-name uniqueness. The agent confirmed buildBaseline does no such check and that uniqueness comes from findGoldenCases' directory listing.
guidance_note: Before a comment names the function that guarantees an invariant, open that function and find the line that enforces it.

evidence: `const os = require('os')` appears in the header hunk, and the agent confirmed with grep that the file never uses os.
guidance_note: Run a lint or unused-import check on new files before opening the PR.

evidence: Under --reuse-candidate nothing is scored, yet the precheck compared expectedMatcherLabel(opts.matcher), defaulting to 'llm', against the baseline, so a lexical reuse would be refused spuriously. compareVerdict already checks the candidate's recorded matcher, so skipping the precheck is correct.
guidance_note: When adding a mode that bypasses a pipeline stage, list every option that only feeds that stage and decide explicitly whether each one is rejected, ignored loudly, or still checked.

evidence: The agent confirmed roundCapReached counts review markers, not SHAs, so a reopen with no new commit spends a round. It declined to change src/transport.js round counting inside an eval PR whose workflow file is generated, and filed copirate-ci-review-lcy. That is a reasonable scope call.

F1's fix tie-broke on generatedAt, which is `provenance.date`, the same YYYY-MM-DD string the dir name is built from, so same-date pairs still always tie. The agent admitted 'my prior fix was cosmetic' and switched to git commit time (%cI) rather than the reviewer's mtime, and that choice then caused F22.
guidance_note: Before claiming a tie-break fix works, write a test that reproduces the exact tie scenario (two same-date baselines) and show it picks the right one.

evidence: F9's fix added the pooled-opportunities throw in compareVerdict without any test, even though every sibling incomparability guard has one in the same test file. The agent added the missing test.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new branch beside siblings that each have a test, add the matching test to the same test block in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows expectedMatcherLabel building `llm/${JUDGE_MODEL}` itself while score.js main() builds the same template inline, so the label format had two producers. Exporting matcherLabel(kind) from score.js gives it one.
guidance_note: When a check must reproduce a value another module writes, import the producer function, not just the constant it interpolates.

evidence: The reuse path derives the candidate engine from the current case.json pin, not from what produced the reused summaries, and the agent agreed this is real. It rejected the meta.json remedy, saying meta.json records the adapter name rather than the provider, but the packet does not show meta.json's shape, so that claim cannot be checked here. It deferred to ticket copirate-eval-provenance-37e without adding even a warning.
guidance_note: When deferring a confirmed silent-wrong-result path, at least make it loud in the meantime (a stderr warning or a usage note) instead of leaving it silent until the ticket lands.

evidence: After F16's fix made matcherLabel the shared producer, compare.js stopped using JUDGE_MODEL, but the export comment still said it existed 'so the compare gate (2fk.5) can build the exact matcher label'. The ac60087 diff rewrites that comment.
guidance_note: When a fix removes a consumer of an export, grep for comments that name that consumer as the export's reason and update them in the same commit.

evidence: F9's fix put the opportunities check only in compareVerdict, after the full replay, in the same commit where F8's fix moved the engine check before spend. The agent admitted it: 'good catch that I didn't apply it here too.' ac60087 adds the 2b pre-pass.
guidance_note: When one fix in a batch establishes a pattern (refuse before spend), apply it to every guard added in that batch before pushing.

evidence: resolveBaselineJsonPath had no test from the original PR onward. The repeated rewrites (F1, F14) motivated the finding but did not create the gap. The ac60087 diff adds real temp-git-repo integration tests, and per the agent one of them caught a same-second tie bug before the push.
guidance_note: Effect code that picks among real artifacts (git history, a directory listing) needs an integration test against a temp fixture in the original PR, and the gitCwd seam that makes that test possible should be added from the start.

evidence: The agent wrote 'imported these anticipating the reuse-mode engine fix, then deferred that fix... without cleaning up the imports'. The findRunDirs and parseMeta imports were residue of the abandoned F17 attempt.
guidance_note: When abandoning a fix attempt, revert every edit the attempt made (imports, exports) before pushing, using a diff of the attempt's commits.

evidence: F14's %cI tie-break sorted a null commit time as `''`, older than any real commit, so a freshly frozen, uncommitted baseline was never picked. Under the earlier name sort that case was never ranked by commit at all. The agent rewrote ranking to commit-graph position with uncommitted ranked newest, instead of using the reviewer's mtime suggestion.
guidance_note: When adding a key that can be null, decide explicitly where null sorts and write the test for that case before relying on a `|| ''` fallback.

evidence: The flagged commit ac60087 does not touch the engine check. The code under review is F8's fix in 4324285, which put the sameEngine check inside the per-case replay loop, so earlier cases replay and score before a later case's drift throws. 255677f moves it into its own 3c pre-pass.
guidance_note: When a fix promises 'before any spend', put the check in a full pre-pass over every item, not inside the loop that spends.

evidence: F21's fix removed the findRunDirs import from compare.js but left the findRunDirs export in score.js, the other half of the same abandoned attempt. The 255677f diff removes it from module.exports.
guidance_note: When cleaning up an abandoned change, check both ends of each cross-module edge it added: the import and the export.

evidence: F19's fix added the 2b pre-loop opportunities sum in main() with no test. 255677f extracts computeExpectedOpportunities and unit-tests it, though the must-find filter still runs inline in main() and stays untested.
guidance_note: When a fix adds logic inside main(), extract the arithmetic as a pure function and test it in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F24 (the same findRunDirs export), raised by a different scope. The agent fixed it once and pointed this thread at that fix.
guidance_note: When abandoning a fix attempt, revert every edit the attempt made (imports, exports) before pushing.

evidence: The DEEPSEEK_API_KEY check runs only inside score.js, after a case's replay has already spent. This is the same spend-before-refusal class that F8's and F19's fixes addressed without sweeping for other instances. The agent extracted requireLlmJudgeCredential but did not act on the finding's second half, the USAGE text, which came back as F36.
guidance_note: After hoisting one pre-spend guard, list every failure the spend loop can hit that is knowable before spending (credentials, file existence, pins) and hoist them all together.

evidence: This is the README side of F23. The reviewer offered either hoisting the check or softening the doc, and the agent took the hoist in 255677f, which makes the README claim true without a doc edit.
guidance_note: When a fix promises 'before any spend', put the check in a full pre-pass over every item, not inside the loop that spends.

evidence: The outcome is real: in a shallow clone, committed baselines tie and fall through to name sort with no warning. The mechanism is wrong, though: the agent's F39 reply found that git reports the same boundary commit for every path, so the ranks tie rather than going null. F22's commit-graph fix only holds with full history, and 255677f adds isShallowRepo and refuses.
guidance_note: When a fix reads git history, run its test against `git clone --depth 1` as well, since CI checkouts are shallow by default.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `candidateRoot = opts.reuseCandidate ? ... : opts.out || ...` expression is unchanged since the original PR (it appears in F8's round-0 hunk), so --out was always silently dropped under reuse. Refusing the combination is correct.
guidance_note: When adding a mode flag that replaces another option's input, reject the conflicting combination in parseArgs instead of letting one option silently win.

evidence: F30's fix refused --out with --reuse-candidate, but --matcher is equally inert under reuse and stayed silent. The reviewer calls it 'the same class of silent-flag-conflict'. The agent made the reuse message state that --matcher is ignored.
guidance_note: When fixing one silently ignored option under a mode, enumerate every option that mode bypasses and handle them all in the same commit.

evidence: F29's fix added a shallow-clone refusal, but the README still described the --baseline default as simply 'newest under eval/baseline/'. With two committed baselines, a default invocation in a fetch-depth 1 checkout now exits 2, which the README never mentioned.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new refusal path to a CLI, update its USAGE text and README flag list in the same commit.

evidence: F30's fix made --out and --reuse-candidate mutually exclusive, and F12's fix made --matcher inert under reuse, but the README flag list still presented them as independent options. The agent documented both behaviors in the README and in USAGE.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new refusal path to a CLI, update its USAGE text and README flag list in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the replay into `--out candidateRoot` and score.js pooling every run dir under it are unchanged since the original PR, so the code only renumbered in 255677f. A reused --out silently blending stale runs is a real pre-existing gap, and refusing instead of auto-cleaning is the right call.
guidance_note: When writing into a caller-named directory that a downstream tool pools wholesale, check it for prior contents before writing.

evidence: F27's fix extracted requireLlmJudgeCredential and made it load-bearing for the pre-spend guard, but the 255677f diff adds no test for it. The agent added a set/unset env test.
guidance_note: When a fix extracts a shared function, add its test in the same commit.

evidence: F27 explicitly said 'The USAGE text (lines 55-56) also doesn't mention that DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is unconditionally required', but the agent's F27 fix only extracted the credential check and left USAGE unchanged. The reviewer had to raise it again.
guidance_note: When a finding has two parts (a code change and a doc change), list both parts in the plan reply and check off each one before replying 'Fixed'.

evidence: 255677f inserted the --out/--reuse refusal as step 1 and renumbered steps 1-5 to 2-6. The untouched '6. Reduce' comment below then duplicated the new '6. Replay' label.
guidance_note: When renumbering a sequence of step comments, grep the whole function for every step number, not just the ones in the diff hunk.

evidence: Before F19's fix, a removed case hit the friendly existsSync message in the replay loop. F19's 2b/3b pre-pass now reads expected.json first with a bare readFileSync, so a removed case throws raw ENOENT and 3c's friendly check never runs.
guidance_note: When moving a read ahead of an existing guard, carry the guard with it or put it in front of the earliest read.

evidence: F29's fix refuses whenever `dirNames.length > 1 && isShallowRepo`, before any ranking. That breaks the uncommitted-plus-committed case, which F22's fix had made decidable (rank -1 always wins). The agent now ranks first and refuses only when the top two tie, and added that test.
guidance_note: Make a refusal guard fire on the actual ambiguity (a tie at the top), not on a proxy like a raw count, and test it against every case the function already decided correctly.

narrative: The PR ran five reviewed rounds and hit the round cap. 21 of the 39 findings exist because of an earlier fix. The baseline tie-break alone took five tries (name sort, generatedAt, commit time, commit graph, shallow refusal, rank-then-refuse), and each fix was claimed before a test reproduced the scenario. Separately, the 'refuse before spend' pattern was applied one guard at a time (engine in-loop, then opportunities post-spend, then credential), so each round found the next unswept instance. Every round still had at least one finding not caused by a fix (F16, F17, F20, F30, F34), so strictly no whole round is avoidable, but most of each round's volume is.
guidance_observations: Fixes were declared done from reasoning alone. The tie-break was rewritten three times before an integration test existed, and once the test was added it immediately caught the next bug.

When a review finding names a class (spend before refusal, a silently ignored flag under reuse), the agent fixed the cited instance only. Sweeping for siblings would have removed most of rounds 2 through 4.
Two-part findings (F27's code plus USAGE) lost their second part between the plan reply and the commit.
An abandoned fix attempt (F17) left residue on both sides of a module edge (an import, then an export), cleaned up over two separate rounds.
